Enquiry 1: Celtic Britain Before the Romans (c. 500 BC – AD 43)

Big Question: Who were the Iron Age Celts, and how did they live before the Roman legions arrived?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Roundhouse (Round-house) Hillfort (Hill-fort) Wattle and Daub (Wat-tle and Daub) Torc (Torc) Druids (Dru-ids)
TASK 1 Primary Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Giant Earth Ramparts of Maiden Castle Hillfort, Dorset (c. 450 BC)
Archaeology Clue: Triple rings of steep chalk ramparts and deep ditches surrounded Iron Age hillforts like Maiden Castle to slow down raiders and guard families and grain stores inside.

1a. Look closely at the steep earth banks and ditches in Source A. How did a hillfort like Maiden Castle help protect a Celtic tribe from raiders?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, the steep earth banks and deep ditches helped protect a Celtic tribe because..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Julius Caesar sails across the Channel twice (55 BC & 54 BC) but returns to Gaul
Celtic tribes dig giant earth ramparts at Maiden Castle Hillfort (c. 450 BC)
Emperor Claudius prepares a full Roman invasion force (AD 43)
Master goldsmiths twist the Snettisham Great Gold Torc (c. 100 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events was the biggest turning point, and why?

✂ Trim along border if sticking into A4 exercise books • The History Revision Hub Page 3 of 16
MISSION 01 CONTINUED • ENQUIRY 1: CELTIC BRITAIN BEFORE THE ROMANS (C. 500 BC – AD 43) PRIMARY RULED WRITING LINES
TASK 3 Historical Investigation • Cause & Consequence

Why did Iron Age builders make roundhouse roofs in a tall cone shape WITHOUT a chimney hole at the top?

Foundation Starter: "Iron Age builders cleverly gave their thatched roundhouses no chimney hole because..."
TASK 4 "Thinking Heads" • Two Different Perspectives
🗣 Person A: Iron Age Celtic Craftworker
Why are you proud of your roundhouse, wheat fields, and gold torcs?
🗣 Person B: Visiting Roman Writer
Why does Britain seem strange compared with stone cities in Rome?
TASK 5 Mission Challenge • Answer Today's Big Enquiry Question

Who were the Iron Age Celts, and how did they live before the Roman legions arrived?

🟢 Foundation Scaffold (Years 3–4): Start with "Before the Roman legions arrived in AD 43, the Iron Age Celts were far from backward because..." • Word Bank: tribes • hillforts • torcs • sea traders
🟣 Scholar Challenge (Year 5+): Weigh up why people once underestimated the Celts — pointing out that Druids memorised knowledge orally instead of leaving written books like the Romans.

Enquiry 2: Why Did Emperor Claudius Invade Britain in AD 43?

Big Question: Why did Emperor Claudius send 40,000 Roman soldiers and war elephants across the sea in AD 43?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Emperor (Em-per-or) Legionary (Le-gion-a-ry) Testudo (Tes-tu-do) Scutum (Scu-tum) Province (Prov-ince)
TASK 1 Primary Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Roman Marble Bust of Emperor Claudius (Reigned AD 41–54)
Museum Clue: Carved first-century marble portrait bust of Emperor Claudius wearing the civic oak-leaf crown (corona civica) to celebrate saving Roman citizens and conquering Britain.

1a. Look at the proud marble statue of Emperor Claudius in Source A. Why did Claudius want Roman people to see him as a mighty conqueror in AD 43?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, Emperor Claudius wore an oak-leaf crown on his marble statue so Romans would see him as..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Emperor Claudius arrives with war elephants to enter Camulodunum (Colchester)
Claudius becomes Emperor in Rome and wants a famous military triumph (AD 41)
Romans win the fierce two-day Battle of the River Medway
40,000 Roman soldiers land at Richborough in Kent (Spring AD 43)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events was the biggest turning point, and why?

✂ Trim along border if sticking into A4 exercise books • The History Revision Hub Page 5 of 16
MISSION 02 CONTINUED • ENQUIRY 2: WHY DID EMPEROR CLAUDIUS INVADE BRITAIN IN AD 43? PRIMARY RULED WRITING LINES
TASK 3 Historical Investigation • Cause & Consequence

Explain TWO big reasons why Emperor Claudius decided to invade Britain in AD 43: one personal reason for Claudius himself, and one reason about Britain's riches.

Foundation Starter: "Emperor Claudius invaded Britain in AD 43 for two big reasons. First, Claudius personally needed..."
TASK 4 "Thinking Heads" • Two Different Perspectives
🗣 Person A: Roman Legionary (AD 43)
Why does your armour, training, and tortoise shield wall make you confident?
🗣 Person B: British Warrior with Caratacus
Why are you determined to defend your tribe from Roman taxes?
TASK 5 Mission Challenge • Answer Today's Big Enquiry Question

Why did Emperor Claudius send 40,000 Roman soldiers and war elephants across the sea in AD 43?

🟢 Foundation Scaffold (Years 3–4): Start with "Emperor Claudius succeeded in conquering southern Britain in AD 43 because Rome arrived prepared with..." • Word Bank: 40,000 soldiers • Richborough • testudo • province
🟣 Scholar Challenge (Year 5+): Use Cassius Dio (Source D) to show that even nervous soldiers who feared sailing "outside the known world" succeeded through planning, supply bases, and Claudius's war elephants at Camulodunum.

Enquiry 3: Boudicca's Rebellion — Why Did the Iceni Rise Up? (AD 60–61)

Big Question: Why did Queen Boudicca lead a huge rebellion against Rome in AD 60, and why did it fail?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Rebellion (Re-bel-lion) Ally (Al-ly) Chariot (Char-i-ot) Destruction Layer (De-struc-tion Lay-er) Archaeologist (Ar-chae-ol-o-gist)
TASK 1 Primary Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Statue of Boudicca in Her Chariot & Tacitus's Account of AD 60 (Events of AD 60 (Annals written c. AD 115))
Tacitus (Annals 14.31): "Kingdom and household alike were plundered like prizes of war... Boudicca was lashed with whips, and the chief men of the Iceni were stripped of their ancestral estates."

1a. Read Tacitus's words in Source A. What had King Prasutagus hoped would happen when he died, and what did Roman officials actually do?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, Tacitus explains that the Iceni rose up in fury because Roman officials..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Governor Suetonius defeats Boudicca in a narrow valley at Watling Street (AD 61)
King Prasutagus dies and Roman officials break his will and seize Iceni land (AD 60)
Londinium and Verulamium burn down into a red clay destruction layer
Boudicca’s warriors march on Camulodunum (Colchester) and burn the Temple of Claudius

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events was the biggest turning point, and why?

✂ Trim along border if sticking into A4 exercise books • The History Revision Hub Page 7 of 16
MISSION 03 CONTINUED • ENQUIRY 3: BOUDICCA'S REBELLION — WHY DID THE ICENI RISE UP? (AD 60–61) PRIMARY RULED WRITING LINES
TASK 3 Historical Investigation • Cause & Consequence

Boudicca had a much bigger army than Governor Suetonius Paulinus! Explain why her rebellion still failed at the Battle of Watling Street in AD 61.

Foundation Starter: "Even though Boudicca had far more warriors, her army lost the Battle of Watling Street because..."
TASK 4 "Thinking Heads" • Two Different Perspectives
🗣 Person A: Iceni Follower of Queen Boudicca
Why did Roman officials leave your tribe no choice except rebellion in AD 60?
🗣 Person B: Shopkeeper in Londinium
What happened to your wooden home and town when Boudicca’s army arrived?
TASK 5 Mission Challenge • Answer Today's Big Enquiry Question

Why did Queen Boudicca lead a huge rebellion against Rome in AD 60, and why did it fail?

🟢 Foundation Scaffold (Years 3–4): Start with "Queen Boudicca's rebellion in AD 60 was caused by cruel Roman greed, and afterwards it changed Roman Britain by..." • Word Bank: Emperor Nero • Londinium • Watling Street • stone walls
🟣 Scholar Challenge (Year 5+): Explain the lasting consequences — rebuilding Colchester and Londinium inside mighty stone walls (Sources B & D) and governing British tribes more carefully so another revolt would not erupt.

Enquiry 4: Hadrian's Wall & Diverse Soldiers on the Frontier (AD 122–400)

Big Question: Why did Emperor Hadrian build a 73-mile stone wall across northern Britain, and who guarded it?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Frontier (Fron-tier) Milecastle (Mile-cas-tle) Latrine (La-trine) Preserved (Pre-served) Auxiliary (Aux-il-ia-ry)
TASK 1 Primary Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Milecastle 39 ('Castle Nick') on Hadrian's Wall, Northumberland (c. AD 122–128)
Frontier Clue: Every Roman mile along the 73-mile stone wall stood a guarded gatehouse (Milecastle) controlling travellers, trade taxes, and raiders crossing the northern frontier.

1a. Look closely at the stone walls and landscape in Source A. How did building Milecastle 39 along steep crags help Roman soldiers control the northern border?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, guarded stone Milecastles along the high crags helped Roman soldiers..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Emperor Hadrian visits Britain and orders a 73-mile stone wall (AD 122)
Claudia Severa sends her wooden birthday party invitation at Vindolanda (c. AD 100)
North African Aurelian Moors guard the frontier fort at Burgh-by-Sands (3rd Century AD)
Syrian trader Barates and British freedwoman Regina live near Arbeia Fort (c. AD 160)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events was the biggest turning point, and why?

✂ Trim along border if sticking into A4 exercise books • The History Revision Hub Page 9 of 16
MISSION 04 CONTINUED • ENQUIRY 4: HADRIAN'S WALL & DIVERSE SOLDIERS ON THE FRONTIER (AD 122–400) PRIMARY RULED WRITING LINES
TASK 3 Historical Investigation • Cause & Consequence

Why did Emperor Hadrian order a 73-mile stone wall with milecastle gates and 16 forts across northern Britain in AD 122?

Foundation Starter: "Emperor Hadrian ordered his legions to build a 73-mile stone wall across northern Britain in AD 122 because..."
TASK 4 "Thinking Heads" • Two Different Perspectives
🗣 Person A: Auxiliary Soldier on Hadrian’s Wall
What is daily life like guarding Milecastles in cold British wind and rain?
🗣 Person B: Northern Farmer Beyond the Wall
How did Hadrian’s stone wall and Milecastle tax gates change your life?
TASK 5 Mission Challenge • Answer Today's Big Enquiry Question

Why did Emperor Hadrian build a 73-mile stone wall across northern Britain, and who guarded it?

🟢 Foundation Scaffold (Years 3–4): Start with "Archaeological clues from Vindolanda and Arbeia prove that Rome's northern frontier was home to a remarkably diverse community because..." • Word Bank: three continents • Aurelian Moors • Barates • Regina
🟣 Scholar Challenge (Year 5+): Conclude how women, children, traders, and freed people in the vici towns show the frontier was far more than an all-male army camp.

Enquiry 5: Life in Roman Towns — Roads, Baths & Villas

Big Question: How did Roman roads, bathhouses, and stone towns transform everyday life in Britain?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Forum (Fo-rum) Aqueduct (Aq-ue-duct) Hypocaust (Hy-po-caust) Strigil (Stri-gil) Mosaic (Mo-sa-ic)
TASK 1 Primary Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Paved Roman Stone Highway over Blackstone Edge, Pennines (1st–2nd Century AD)
Engineering Clue: Roman surveyors stacked gravel and gently curved (cambered) stone slabs between deep side ditches so rainwater drained away and heavy supply carts never sank.

1a. Look closely at the stone surface and shape of the road in Source A. How was a Roman highway an improvement on muddy Iron Age tracks?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, gently curved stone highways with side ditches helped armies and carts travel because..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Wealthy Romano-British elites lay colourful dolphin mosaic floors in grand villas
Roman surveyors sight straight routes and soldiers lay cambered stone highways
Most countryside families continue farming wheat around thatched roundhouses
Aqueducts pipe clean spring water into town fountains and Aquae Sulis baths

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events was the biggest turning point, and why?

✂ Trim along border if sticking into A4 exercise books • The History Revision Hub Page 11 of 16

TASK 3 Historical Investigation • Cause & Consequence

How did Roman engineers build roads and water systems that transformed travel and hygiene in British towns?

Foundation Starter: "Roman engineers transformed travel and town hygiene across Britain by building..."
TASK 4 "Thinking Heads" • Two Different Perspectives
🗣 Person A: Wealthy Villa Owner
How have hypocaust heating, mosaics, and steam baths changed your life?
🗣 Person B: Countryside Roundhouse Farmer

TASK 5 Mission Challenge • Answer Today's Big Enquiry Question

How did Roman roads, bathhouses, and stone towns transform everyday life in Britain?

🟣 Scholar Challenge (Year 5+): Explain how even countryside farmers in roundhouses still felt Roman rule through Roman roads and paying Roman taxes.

Enquiry 6: Farewell to the Legions — What Was Rome's Lasting Legacy? (AD 410 & Beyond)

Big Question: Why did the Roman army leave Britain around AD 410, and what did the Romans leave behind for us today?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Hoard (Hoard) Legacy (Leg-a-cy) Castra (Cas-tra) Latin (Lat-in) Roman Numerals (Ro-man Nu-mer-als)
TASK 1 Primary Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Gold Solidus Coin of Emperor Honorius & Zosimus's Account of AD 410 (c. AD 395–410)
Zosimus (New History 6.10, AD 410): With enemy armies attacking Italy and Gaul, "Honorius wrote letters to the cities in Britain, bidding them to guard themselves."

1a. Read the translated line from Zosimus alongside Emperor Honorius's gold coin in Source A. Why couldn't Honorius send fresh legions to protect Britain in AD 410?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, Emperor Honorius could not send fresh soldiers to defend Britain in AD 410 because..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Farmers rediscover the buried Hoxne and Mildenhall silver hoards centuries later
Picts, Scotti, and Saxons raid Britain while enemy armies threaten Italy (c. AD 400)
Anxious Romano-British families bury chests of silver plates and pepper pots
Emperor Honorius tells British towns they must look to their own defences (AD 410)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events was the biggest turning point, and why?

✂ Trim along border if sticking into A4 exercise books • The History Revision Hub Page 13 of 16
